Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
301 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Subtle adjustments in regards to temperatures today and 
precipitation chances Thursday and Friday. Otherwise, current 
forecast remains on track. 


&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Above normal temperatures continue with the first rain chances 
in two weeks Thursday and Friday.

- 2) Cooler temperatures and mountain showers expected this
  weekend as another strong front crosses early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures continue with the first 
rain chances in two weeks Thursday and Friday.

Broad high pressure over the western Atlantic will continue to 
maintain above normal temperatures and quiet conditions through this 
evening. Expect light winds out of the south and southeast (gusting 
15-20 mph) yielding highs for most in the low to mid 70s. A few 
locations could punch into the upper 70s in the lee of Alleghenies 
and south/east of Washington, D.C. this afternoon given increased 
southerly flow.  After some patchy fog to start, expect mostly sunny 
skies to prevail giving way to increasing cloud cover during the 
afternoon and evening as the incumbent trough/front approach from 
the Ohio River Valley. 

After a 2+ week hiatus, rain chances return from the west late 
tonight into Thursday and Friday. This is largely due in part to the 
ridge of high pressure shunting east and an incumbent trough/front 
entering from the upper Great Lakes and Ohio River Valley. Model 
consensus continues to trend downward on widespread rain chances 
with this system given the bulk of the forcing north and west of the 
region. Most of the guidance has low pressure ejecting out of the 
northern Great Lakes into eastern Ontario with it's associated cold 
front ejecting from the Ohio River Valley Thursday morning into 
Thursday afternoon. The front will stall along and east of I-95 
Thursday night into Friday. Another area of low pressure will 
develop along the front down across the Carolinas riding north to 
the Delmarva and southern New England coast Friday afternoon into 
Saturday morning. As a result, expect the greatest rain chances 
along west of the Alleghenies and in areas along/east of I-95 with 
somewhat of a skip in between. Rainfall amounts will range between a 
quarter to a half an inch areawide through Friday with locally 
heavier totals along and east of I-95 (southern MD) as well as over 
the mountains. Highs will remain in the upper 60s and low 70s 
Thursday and Friday despite the added cloud cover (low 60s 
mountains). West to northwest flow may contribute to some 
downsloping east of the mountains leading to the warmer conditions. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures and mountain showers expected 
this weekend as another strong front crosses early next week. 

One upper level trough exits with a more potent one to follow toward 
the back half of the weekend into early next week. Upslope showers 
may linger over the mountains and in locations east of I-95 Saturday 
morning as the upper level trough/cold front push offshore. Weak 
high pressure will build from the south Saturday afternoon into 
Sunday ahead of a more pedant trough heading into the first half of 
next week. Once again the main forcing with this system will be up 
toward the Hudson Bay of Canada while the resultant surface fronts 
cross the region. Overall guidance has trended downward in 
precipitation with this system with any shower chances Sunday and 
Monday confined to the mountains. These areas have a better bet of 
precipitation given the terrain influence compared to the locations 
further east where any mentionable forcing is lacking. Broad 1020-
1022 mb high pressure builds back in from the southeastern US Monday 
into Tuesday with another cold front to follow by the middle of next 
week. Overall synoptic pattern turns zonal for much of next week. 

Seasonable temperatures are expected to return this weekend and into 
much of next week. Highs will settle back into the upper 50s and mid 
60s (40s mountains). Overnight lows will fall back into the 30s and 
40s. 

&&

.AVIATION /08Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions will continue through tonight outside of some patchy 
sub-VFR vsbys from fog this morning. Winds will remain out of the 
south and southeast with occasional gusts between 15-20 kts this 
afternoon and evening. High pressure pushing offshore and an 
incumbent cold front/trough from the west will yield in the uptick 
in winds this afternoon. Any patchy fog will occur through 13z/8am 
this morning before quickly burning off just beyond sunrise. The 
greatest confidence for fog will be at terminals along and east of I-
95, in particularly close to waters. 

VFR conditions continue into Thursday although brief sub-VFR 
reductions are possible at times with showers Thursday morning into 
Thursday afternoon. PROB30s will be added between 06-18z time window 
for the greatest coverage of showers as the front pushes across. 
Additional PROB30S/prevailing lines will be needed for rain chances 
Thursday night into Friday as the front stalls in the vicinity of 
the I-95 corridor terminals. South to southwesterly winds continue 
at less than 15 kts. 

Additional sub-VFR reductions are possible at times Friday into 
Saturday as a secondary trough of low pressure moves along the 
stalled front to the east of the corridor. Winds will shift to the 
west Friday and eventually northwest Friday night into Saturday. VFR 
conditions return Saturday into Sunday with another round of sub-VFR 
conditions late Sunday into Monday as a secondary cold front pushes 
through. 

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through this morning. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast as high pressure pushes 
offshore. By this afternoon into Thursday, expect the potential for 
southerly channeling due to the high offshore and incumbent trough 
from the northern Ohio River Valley. Confidence in this occurring is 
low with a focus over the middle and open waters. 

Low pressure and a strong cold front will work across the waters 
Thursday into Friday. Widespread showers and perhaps a few 
thunderstorms are possible Thursday afternoon through Friday 
afternoon. Winds will remain around SCA levels both days with west 
to northwest gusts up to 20 kts. Weak high pressure returns Saturday 
before another strong front crosses late Sunday into Monday. This 
front will bring a greater likelihood of SCA conditions across the 
waters heading into early next week.
